source_text: Adeste igitur, vos quoque carissimi, et dulcia verba illa ex spiritali David cithara nobis repraesentata decantemus, dicentes: Surge Domine, in requiem tuam: tu, et arca sanctificationis tuae. Vere enim arca est sanctissima Virgo; intrinsecus et extrinsecus deaurata, quae universum sanctificationis thesaurum suscepit. Surge Domine, in requiem tuam. Surge Domine, ex sinu Patris, ut collapsum primi parentis genus erigas.
thought_title: Call to sing of the Lord entering his rest
orientation: After recounting Gabriel coming to Mary, the preacher now urges the hearers to sing David's oracle about the Lord and the ark.
pass_a_gloss: Come here therefore, you also, beloved, and let us sing those sweet words set before us from the spiritual harp of David, saying: Arise Lord into your rest, you and the ark of your sanctification. For in truth the most holy Virgin is the ark, gilded within and without, who received the whole treasure of sanctification. Arise Lord into your rest. Arise Lord from the bosom of the Father, in order that you may raise up the fallen race of the first parent.

choices.english: from the spiritual harp of David
choices.why: keeps the instrumental source image and the adjective with David, not a general spiritual song
literal genitive as written, preserving the source noun rather than importing strength from Hebrew
keeps both adverbs and the passive participle exactly
rejected: overlaid with gold inside and out

choices.english: from the bosom of the Father
choices.why: sinus here is bosom as place of origin, not merely presence

choices.english: fallen race of the first parent
choices.why: genus is race or offspring and primus parens is left unnamed as in the source

bible_refs.note: quoted source words Surge Domine, in requiem tuam: tu, et arca sanctificationis tuae; LXX numbering is Psalms 131:8

pass_b_english: So come, you also, my beloved, and let us sing those sweet words set before us from the spiritual harp of David, saying: "Rise up, Lord, to your resting place, you and the ark of your sanctification" (Psalm 132:8). For the most holy Virgin is truly that ark, gilded within and without, who received the whole treasure of sanctification.
Rise up, Lord, to your resting place. Rise up, Lord, from the bosom of the Father, to lift up the fallen race of the first parent.
